## Blocking Findings

### [requirements] Merge re-adds the `strike.ts` baseline row that PAN-4258 removed — `scripts/lint-effort.sh:39`
- Severity: `!` (failure of an explicit in-scope acceptance criterion)
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect (merge-resolution regression); in_pr_scope
- Trigger and changed-code connection: PAN-4258 (5ea1be0ed74, on main) removed `["src/cli/commands/strike.ts"]=1  # PAN-4259` after fixing strike.ts. This branch's W10 commit d5d5deb1d56 was written while main still had the row; merge 955bbbd51d3 kept the branch side. Proof: the row count is 0 at merge-base 832b65e07ca, 0 at origin/main, 0 at 955bbbd51d3^2 (main side), 1 at 955bbbd51d3^1 and at HEAD. `git diff 832b65e07ca..HEAD -- scripts/lint-effort.sh` shows the row as a `+` line, so this PR adds it.
- Expected / observed / impact: AC-10 requires that `bash scripts/lint-effort.sh` "exits 0, prints no `note: lower BASELINE` line". Observed: it exits 0 but prints `note: lower BASELINE[src/cli/commands/strike.ts] to 0`. Commit 607a4961ded nevertheless recorded w10-lint-effort-baseline.ac1/ac2 as done. Beyond the AC, the merge reopens a ratchet slot: one `?? 'high'` fallback or level-list copy could return to strike.ts and the lint would still pass. CI cannot catch this because the script exits 0 on a lowerable baseline.
- Evidence: `bash scripts/lint-effort.sh` run locally at HEAD (output above); `git show <rev>:scripts/lint-effort.sh | grep -c strike` for the revisions listed.
- Fix: delete the `["src/cli/commands/strike.ts"]=1  # PAN-4259` line from `BASELINE`, re-run `bash scripts/lint-effort.sh`, and confirm it prints no `note:` line.

## Non-blocking Findings

### [requirements] gpt-5.5 `max→xhigh` (D6/F5) was dropped — specification defect, not an implementation failure — `src/lib/model-capabilities.ts:598`
- Severity: `~`
- Classification: specification defect; in_pr_scope (spec text), whole_feature_scope (residual)
- The PRD's AC-2 says codex.test.ts "passes with the gpt-5.6-sol identity table and the gpt-5.5 `max→xhigh` row", and AC-3 (W3 step 3) asks for "with `gpt-5.5`, `max` yields `--effort 'xhigh'`". Neither the row nor these tests exist. The implementer documented why in commit 1527d8f916c, and I verified the reason: `getModelEffortLevels` (`model-capabilities.ts:1397-1399`) calls `resolveModelId`, which maps through `MODEL_DEPRECATIONS` (`model-deprecations.ts:19`: `'gpt-5.5': 'gpt-5.6-sol'`) before the row lookup. So an `effortLevels` value on the `gpt-5.5` row is never read for clamping, and the F5 premise is stale. The CodeRabbit comment on `.pan/drafts/PAN-4260.md:319` points at the same mismatch.
- Spec correction: retire D6 and the gpt-5.5 clauses of AC-2/AC-3 in the PRD/xBRIEF, noting that gpt-5.5 inherits gpt-5.6-sol's levels. The docs already match the code: effort.mdx dropped "GPT-5.5 stops at xhigh", and harnesses.mdx states the alias caveat.
- Residual (pre-existing, unverified): the implementer notes that an explicit `--model gpt-5.5` launch with `max` can still reach Codex as `max`, because `requireModelOverride` does not resolve deprecated ids. This PR does not introduce it, and I did not trace whether Codex rejects it. It belongs in a follow-up issue if the operator wants it.

### [correctness] Claude Code role-definition branch emits `--effort` without clamping — `src/lib/agents/runtime-command.ts:853-854`
- Severity: `?`
- Classification: pre-existing issue; out of FR-1's producer list (claude-code launch surfaces are owned by PAN-4256/4257)
- `roleSystemPromptInjection` pushes `--effort ${explicitEffort ?? frontmatter.effort}` without calling `resolveEffort`. Only the definition-less branch (line 941) clamps. The new claude-code mapping table deliberately uses sub-role `security` so that it exercises the clamping branch (the test comment says so). The harnesses.mdx row "max (clamped to the model, e.g. Sonnet 4.6 `xhigh`→`high`)" therefore holds only where callers pass an already-resolved value. Evidence limit: I did not trace whether every caller of the definition branch passes a pre-resolved effort.

### [requirements] OpenCode models without an effort option now fail on a non-`high` role effort (H7)
- Severity: `?`
- Classification: intended behavior per the spec (D2/H7); noted for operator awareness
- `getAcpLauncherFields` now reads `role` (it was `_role`) and always returns a resolved `acpEffort`. With `roles.<role>.effort: low|medium` on an OpenCode model that exposes no `effort` config option, `acp/host.ts` throws `does not expose an effort setting` at session start, where such an agent used to start. The PRD's H7 explicitly accepts this. Conversations already resolved effort before this PR, so it changes nothing for them.

### [process] Working-tree modification not in HEAD
- `.pan/continues/PAN-4260.xbrief.json` is modified but uncommitted in the workspace. This review covers committed HEAD only.

### Caller sweep for the new D2 throws (non-test src)
- `resolveKimiNativeEffort`: runtimes/acp.ts:205 (resolved value), acp/host.ts:177 (launcher always passes `--effort` now), acp/host.ts:359 (`op.effort.trim()`, defined), launcher-generator.ts:894/972 (fed by producers that always resolve).
- `piEffort`/`museEffort`/`codexEffort` producers: runtime-command.ts:113/177, runtimes/ohmypi.ts:350, runtimes/muse.ts:96, spawn.ts:338, spawn-prep.ts:745, spawn-planning-session.ts:630, conversation-runtime.ts:605/663/696 (`launchEffort` comes from `resolveConversationEffort`, which always returns a string). None can pass undefined.
- `initCodexHome`: codex.ts:661, runtime-command.ts:193, conversation-runtime.ts:681. All pass effort, and typecheck enforces it.
- `AcpRuntimeSync.spawnAgent` `resolveEffort` cannot receive an OpenCode variant: `SpawnConfig.effort` is `EffortLevel`, and relaunch callers go through `resolveRelaunchEffort`, which returns only canonical levels.

- Security: no new trust boundary. `set-effort` validation is now `isEffortLevel` (stricter than or equal to before); effort values still pass through `shellQuote`. No findings.
- Performance: `resolveEffort` is a synchronous config read per launch, not in a hot loop. No findings.
- Requirements/UX: AC matrix below. Docs updated as required.
